pitch_detail.notes: Cross Quien Sabe Glacier, rappel into and cross the Boston Glacier to the Boston-Forbidden col
Short, steep left-facing corner from the col
Ridge crest past a wildly exposed bivy platform
Above ~8,400 ft, steeper terrain on notably better rock to the summit block
Loose scrambling and a steep open chimney to start.
Confusing routefinding, relentless exposure through sandy gullies and loose rock.
Rocky towers culminate in an old-school face traverse protected by a single in-situ piton.
Chimney climbing and more moderate pitches.
Three long, loose simul-climbing pitches lead to the summit.
Boston Basin camp to glacier toe, roped up before stepping on ice.
Left side is broken but moderate; right side is steeper with more crevasse exposure.
Ice axe/crampons for the ridge traverse, then loose rock scramble to the top.
Ascends from the avalanche-fan base; crevasses begin to appear.
~300 vertical ft, only 20-50 ft wide; water ice near the top may require a belay.
Multiple crevasse crossings; snow bridges vary by season and time of day.
Broken gneiss rock pitches, gullies and ribs; first gully has the best rock quality.
Significant exposure; a two-person bivy site sits about 30 minutes from the summit.
Downclimb into the avalanche moat to gain the rock; initial 4th-class terrain into dense tree climbing.
Vertical tree-root and brush climbing.
Slabby gully traverse, roughly 60 ft horizontal, minimal protection.
Steep heather terrain requiring careful footwork.
Crux section of sustained, higher-quality rock climbing, roughly 700 ft.
Upper ridge and summit scramble past the glacier-adjacent bivy site, two pitches below the top.
Clean arete descending NE from the main ridge, simul-climbed to an 8,200-ft tower, then one rappel.
Running-belay climbing along the crest toward the SE Peak.
Three long pitches; easier options exist further left.
Above the Goode Glacier near Black Tooth Notch, with an icy moat to negotiate.
